racing-red.purpose: Accent fill in both themes: the Next chip, primary buttons, favicon tile, checked radio, selection tint.

racing-red-text-dark.purpose: Red as text on dark: wordmark second word, Next marker, row month, caret.

racing-red-text-light.purpose: Red as text on light, deepened for contrast.

garage-graphite.purpose: Dark card, row, field and sheet surface.

raised-graphite.purpose: Dark raised layer: countdown cells, session codes, current row, hover fills.

timing-white.purpose: Dark primary text, countdown numbers, circuit stroke.

telemetry-grey.purpose: Dark secondary text and icons at rest.

quiet-grey.purpose: Dark tertiary text: placeholders, finished items.

paper-white.purpose: Light card, row, field and sheet surface.

timing-ink.purpose: Light primary text and circuit stroke.

live-tint-dark.purpose: Background behind live chips, tags and code blocks on dark.

live-tint-light.purpose: Background behind live elements on light.

amber-tint-dark.purpose: Background behind the Starting soon chip on dark.

amber-tint-light.purpose: Background behind the Starting soon chip on light.

themes.switching: System by default; a header switch and a System / Light / Dark setting store the choice in localStorage (f1-theme), applied as data-theme on <html> before first paint.

headline.purpose: Grand Prix name on the featured card, balanced wrap.

wordmark.purpose: F1 Calendar in the header; second word in Racing Red Text.

row-title.purpose: Weekend names in the season list; 550 and secondary once finished.

time.purpose: Session start times; 500 and tertiary once done.

body.purpose: 15px on phones, 16px from 720px; whole calendar is tabular-nums.

meta.purpose: Row meta, schedule notes, weather, footer.

label.purpose: Uppercase day headings; month labels use 11px with 0.06em tracking.

shadows.name: segment-selected
shadows.purpose: Checked option in the theme segmented control.

motion.name: ease-out

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Colour and background transitions on rows, icon buttons, fields, buttons (brightness 1.08).

motion.name: track-draw

motion.name: sheet-out

narrative.overview:
F1 Calendar looks the way a fan expects an F1 schedule product to look, and is built better than the ones they already use. It is the category standard, chosen on purpose and played straight: flat cards on a calm tinted ground, one racing-red accent of our own, big tabular numbers for the countdown, and the circuit drawing as the only illustration. There is no novelty world and no smuggled quirk. The ambition lives in the finish: even spacing, numbers that never jitter, 44px tap targets, short purposeful motion, and two themes that are equally considered.

The page answers one question first: what is next, and when, in my timezone. The featured card for the next weekend owns the top of the page (Grand Prix name, a status chip, a day/hour/minute countdown, the circuit drawing, and the weekend's sessions by day with weather). Everything else recedes: the season list is a compact dated list of rows, finished weekends stay in place and dim, and the weekend detail opens in a sheet (a centred modal on desktop, a bottom sheet on phones). Density is generous on the featured card and compact in the list.

Light and dark are equals. The page follows the system theme by default; a header switch sets a remembered manual choice (stored before first paint, so there is no flash), and settings offer System, Light and Dark. Each theme has its own tinted neutrals and its own accent-text and state shades tuned for contrast; neither is a filter over the other.
keyCharacteristics: The category standard, executed carefully: familiar layout, no gimmicks.
One focus per screen: the featured next-weekend card leads, the season list recedes.
Tabular figures everywhere, so times and the countdown never jitter.
The single-stroke circuit drawing is the only illustration, and the only thing that draws itself in.
Flat tonal layering; a shadow appears only on the open sheet and the selected segment.
First-class light and dark themes, system-driven with a remembered switch.
Motion is short and purposeful, or absent; all of it stops under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Red Fill Rule
rules.body: Racing Red fills one thing per view: the Next chip on the featured card, or the primary action of a panel. Red as text marks identity (the wordmark) and "what's next" (the next session, the date blocks), never decoration.

rules.name: The State Colour Rule
rules.body: Green means live now, amber means starting soon, and red is never a state colour. Finished sessions and weekends are shown by dimming to tertiary text, not by colour.

rules.name: The Twin Theme Rule
rules.body: Every colour token has a value for both themes. Accent text, state colours, focus and the sheet shadow are re-tuned for light, not reused.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: The whole calendar and the sheet set `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so digits never shift while the countdown ticks and times line up in columns.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Chips, tags, buttons and countdown units are sentence or lower case. Uppercase is reserved for the day headings and the month in date blocks.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards and rows sit flat on the ground. Lift is a response to state (an open sheet, a selected segment), never decoration, and never a glow.

dos: Do follow the system theme by default, offer a header switch and a System / Light / Dark setting, and apply the stored choice before first paint.
Do define every colour for both themes and re-tune accent text, state colours, focus and shadows for light.
Do keep the featured next-weekend card as the only focused card, with its status chip, countdown, circuit drawing and schedule.
Do set every time, date and countdown in tabular figures, and show each session time with its weekday and timezone.
Do use Racing Red (#c8232f) for fills and Racing Red Text for red words, never Formula 1's #E10600.
Do keep tap targets at 44px (extend a compact control's hit area when needed) and show focus with the 2px Focus Blue outline.
Do dim finished sessions and weekends in place rather than hiding or recolouring them.
Do keep motion short and purposeful, on transform and opacity, and turn all of it off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do show weather only where it is real data, and label missing data plainly ("Times TBC", "Track layout unavailable").
donts: Don't imitate Formula 1's brand: no exact F1 red (#E10600), no F1 logo, no imitation of its proprietary typeface.
Don't use red for state: live is green, soon is amber, done is dimmed.
Don't add shadows to cards or rows, or any glow; depth is tonal.
Don't use gamer or neon styling: no glowing edges or neon accents.
Don't ship cheap animation: no bounces, no long fades, no decorative motion on every element, nothing that stutters on a phone.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above headings; the Grand Prix name leads its card.
Don't clutter the phone view: one focus, a clear list, and nothing that slows down the answer to "what is next and when".
